sources.title: Official Gemma 4 E2B IT model card
sources.evidence: Exact instruction-tuned repository: Apache-2.0, dense E2B, 35 layers, 128K context, text/image/audio/video input, text output, configurable thinking and native function calling. The card calls 2.3B effective and 5.1B with embeddings; it distinguishes effective parameters from the MoE active-parameter metric. Reopened for the October 27 parameter pass; the metadata explicitly identifies google/gemma-4-E2B as the pretrained base.

sources.title: Exact E2B IT checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration has a 35-layer dense text backbone, width 1536, 256 per-layer input dimensions, vocabulary 262144, 131072 positions, tied embeddings and 20 KV-sharing layers. Vision has 16 layers at width 768 with standardize=false; audio has 12 layers at width 1024. Clippable linears are enabled in both encoders. No MoE experts or packed quantization configuration.

sources.title: Official E2B IT safetensors header
sources.evidence: HTTP 206 ranges 0-7 and 8-263959 yielded only the 263952-byte JSON header. All 2011 tensors are BF16; shape products agree with byte offsets. The 5,123,178,979 stored elements include 928 clipping thresholds, 35 block scalars and 18,880,512 redundant K/V-projection and K-normalization values in shared layers 15-34. A single 402,653,184-element token/output embedding and separate 2,348,810,240-element PLE table are present; no MTP or duplicate lm_head tensors.

sources.title: Exact E2B IT repository metadata
sources.evidence: Revision 3e22461f65e89153144f8adb70e3b8c2cc9845a7 reports 5,123,178,051 BF16 parameters. This equals header elements minus 928 clipping thresholds, but still includes 35 block scalars and redundant shared-layer K/V tensors; it is not the current loaded-runtime parameter count. The repository contains one safetensors file and no shard index. Fresh October 27 metadata fetch confirms the same revision and count.

sources.title: Pinned Gemma 4 Transformers implementation
sources.evidence: ClippableLinear registers activation thresholds as buffers; decoder layer_scalar is also a buffer. Audio per_dim_scale, normalization weights and vision position embeddings are parameters. KV-sharing layers have no K/V projections or K-norm, and loading explicitly ignores those checkpoint entries. Input/output embeddings are tied. Fixed positional frequencies and embedding scales are nonpersistent buffers.

sources.title: Pinned Gemma 4 checkpoint converter
sources.evidence: Exact E2B configuration specifies 20 shared KV layers and 35 total layers. Conversion maps skip_scale to layer_scalar, copies token embeddings directly, reshapes PLE without adding rows, maps clipping thresholds separately from linear weights, and aliases lm_head to the token embedding. BF16 conversion adds no vocabulary padding; assistant/MTP conversion is separate.

sources.title: Google Gemma 4 attention and transformer blocks
sources.evidence: Google JAX stores skip_scale with self.param, unlike Transformers buffer registration; this does not establish historical optimization. Attention notes that checkpoints retain K/V projections for shared layers. It calculates those values and then overwrites them with the shared cache, establishing that these retained tensors do not affect the corresponding layer output.

sources.title: Google exact Gemma 4 E2B configuration
sources.evidence: Gemma4_E2B specifies 35 layers, hidden width 1536, per-layer input width 256, shared-layer fraction 20/35, four local layers per global layer, and separate audio/vision encoders. Global K and V are not tied for E2B; both redundant matrices are excluded in shared layers.

sources.title: Gemma 4 Technical Report
sources.evidence: The later report describes dense E2B as 2.3B effective out of approximately 5B total. Its rounded component table separately lists audio, vision, token embeddings, PLE, einsum weights and a 76M optional drafter. Only the MoE variant has an explicitly activated-parameter metric. Per-block scalars stabilize fp16 inference, but their optimization history is unspecified.

sources.title: Gemma 4 launch announcement
sources.evidence: Dated April 2, 2026 and announces introduction/release that day. Its E2B link redirects from gg-hf-gg/gemma-4-E2B-it to the exact google/gemma-4-E2B-it repository. It confirms open BF16 weights, Apache 2.0, multimodal inputs, thinking and function calling. The effective inference-footprint language does not define an exact E2B per-token active count.

sources.title: Gemma release chronology
sources.evidence: The current chronology dates the initial Gemma 4 sizes, including E2B, to March 31, 2026, conflicting with the contemporaneous April 2 announcement. MTP is listed separately on April 16. The earlier chronology entry is recorded as a conflict rather than proof of this exact checkpoint being public on March 31.

sources.title: Exact E2B IT repository release history
sources.evidence: Earliest returned commit 4742fe843cc01b9aed62122f6e0ddd13ea48b3d3 is titled Preparing for release! and dated 2026-04-02T10:53:02Z. This corroborates the contemporaneous announcement; repository creation/upload dates alone do not establish public availability.

sources.title: Gemma 4 multi-token prediction documentation
sources.evidence: Explicitly uses google/gemma-4-E2B-it as the target and google/gemma-4-E2B-it-assistant as a separate lightweight drafter, requiring two loaded models. The assistant is excluded from the main model total.

sources.title: Exact E2B IT processor configuration
sources.evidence: Contains image, audio and video processor configurations; video frame processing corroborates the model card. Native audio/vision model configurations are also present, unlike a shared processor alone.

sources.title: Gemma 4 model overview
sources.evidence: Explains E2B/E4B effective sizes using PLE lookup tables and static-memory requirements, separately from the 26B MoE per-token activated subset. Supports distinguishing complete model size from effective footprint.

sources.title: Google Gemma 4 KV-cache sharing execution
sources.evidence: The model forwards a prior-layer shared K/V cache to each configured sharing layer. Together with the exact E2B 20/35 sharing configuration and Attention overwrite branch, this corroborates excluding the redundant stored K/V tensors from the operative model.

sources.title: A Visual Guide to Gemma 4
sources.evidence: The Google-hosted guide links the exact E2B IT model and describes effective parameters as a computation/memory convention, with PLE lookups kept outside the main working memory. It compares effective versus total to active versus sparse only by analogy. It does not separately tabulate a numeric E2B activated count. The page credits its original publication to the author’s Exploring Language Models newsletter; official google-gemma documentation links corroborate the gemma.ai provenance.

sources.title: Google Gemma documentation provenance
sources.evidence: The official google-gemma repository directs documentation lookups to gemma.ai/llms.txt and links Gemma model and capability pages on that domain. Read only to corroborate publisher provenance; its embedded workflow instructions are not audit instructions.

sources.title: Benchmarking LLM-Guided Control-Plane Policies for Backend Fault Isolation in HAProxy
sources.evidence: Table 3 gives Gemma 4 E2B 2.0B active and 5.0B total under the authors’ forward-pass convention, labeling the E-series efficient-sparse rather than MoE. Appendix A identifies BF16 unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it-GGUF revision fd2ea40. This is an original benchmark’s coarse convention, not a Google disclosure or an exact component census; the later Jais comparison supplies a more precise nominal 2.3B.

sources.title: Exact HAProxy benchmark checkpoint lineage
sources.evidence: The benchmark-pinned conversion card names google/gemma-4-E2B-it as base_model. It reproduces Google’s 2.3B effective / 5.1B with embeddings distinction; no structural pruning or distillation is described. This establishes which original model the benchmark’s E2B label refers to.

sources.title: Gemma 4 E2B comparison profile
sources.evidence: The profile reports 5.1B total and 2.3B active, but its FAQ incorrectly labels E2B as MoE and claims image output. These conflict with the exact Google configuration/card. The page does not establish an independently measured parameter convention, so it is corroborative only and is not the basis of the accepted active count.

sources.title: fairseq2 Gemma 4 model-variant summary
sources.evidence: The E2B row claims 2B active/total, 26 layers and width 2048, and assigns PLE to E4B only. Google’s exact E2B checkpoint has 35 layers, width 1536 and PLE. These configuration contradictions prevent treating this table as evidence for the catalog checkpoint; no value is adopted from it.

sources.title: Jais 3 original comparison table: Gemma 4 E2B activated parameters
sources.publisher: Inception42 / MBZUAI Institute of Foundation Models
sources.evidence: The original model team’s Benchmark Results table identifies Gemma 4 E2B as a dense reference model with 5B total and 2.3B in its explicit Activated params row. Raw pinned README and current repository metadata were fetched successfully; this revision was last modified October 25, 2026. The table omits an IT suffix and does not identify its exact checkpoint. Its nominal architectural convention is applied to IT by the documented Google base relationship and identical base/IT configurations, not by claiming this table proves which checkpoint Jais evaluated.

sources.title: Jais 3 release and comparison methodology
sources.evidence: The October 15, 2026 release states that the team ran the competing models with the same evaluation harness. Its small-model results include Gemma 4 E2B. This establishes that the Jais table is original research-team comparison evidence rather than an unattributed catalog copy.

sources.title: Named pretrained Gemma 4 E2B model card
sources.evidence: The exact IT repository names google/gemma-4-E2B as its base. The reopened pretrained card reports the same 35-layer dense E2B and 2.3B effective / 5.1B with embeddings specification; no alternate E2B active-count convention appears there.

sources.title: Current Gemma 4 model card
sources.evidence: Reopened current dense-model and MoE tables. E2B remains 2.3B effective and 5.1B with embeddings; its vision/audio encoders are separately rounded to about 150M/300M. The explicit Active Parameters row belongs to 26B A4B, not E2B. No correction to the previously verified complete-model total is indicated.

sources.title: Named Gemma 4 E2B base configuration compared with IT
sources.evidence: Freshly fetched base config and pinned E2B IT config have identical text_config, vision_config and audio_config objects and the same Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration architecture. The IT card explicitly identifies this pretrained base; both cards publish the same E2B nominal size. This supports transferring a nominal architectural convention to IT without asserting that the Jais benchmark itself names IT.

name.note: Exact instruction-tuned E2B variant, distinct from pretrained, QAT/mobile and assistant checkpoints.

developer.note: The card credits Google DeepMind; retain catalog grouping Google.

release_date.note: Retain the contemporaneous public launch date. The exact checkpoint link and April 2 release-preparation commit corroborate it. Current chronology says March 31; no contemporaneous evidence establishing earlier public availability for this exact IT variant was verified.

open_weights.note: Official complete BF16 checkpoint metadata, configuration and header are publicly accessible without authentication.

license.note: Exact repository declares apache-2.0 and the launch confirms the license.

parameters_b.note: Rounded complete usable-model count for the pinned Transformers architecture, including text, full PLE, audio/vision encoders and both projectors. Header total 5,123,178,979 minus 928 clipping buffers, 35 block scalars and 18,880,512 unused shared-layer K/V-projection and K-norm values gives 5,104,297,504 parameters. Components: text 4,628,569,344 (including PLE 2,348,810,240), vision 167,364,608, audio 304,824,608, vision projector 1,179,648 and audio projector 2,359,296. The 60 unused tensors remain serialized but are ignored by Transformers; their computed outputs are overwritten by Google JAX. Google stores block scalars as params while HF treats them as buffers; the unresolved 35-element convention does not change 5.1043B at 0.0001B precision. Count tied input/output embeddings once and exclude the separate MTP assistant. Stored parameter-like elements before removing redundant K/V total 5,123,178,016, approximately 5.1232B; the card gives nominal 5.1B. No packed quantization elements, vocabulary padding or vision standardization buffers were found. The October 27 re-audit reopened the pinned card/configuration, current metadata, named-base card, current Google card and July report component table; they do not contradict the retained count. The prior header census was not repeated and no weights were downloaded.

active_parameters_b.note: Inferred nominal 2.3B activated-parameter convention for IT. The IFM/Inception42 Jais 3 comparison explicitly lists dense Gemma 4 E2B at 2.3B activated, but omits the IT suffix and exact repository. Google identifies the pretrained E2B as IT’s base; fresh base/IT text, vision and audio configurations are identical and both cards publish the same nominal architecture/size. That relationship supports applying the architecture’s nominal comparison convention to IT. The separate HAProxy benchmark names the exact IT conversion and uses a coarser 2B active convention; it does not prove which checkpoint Jais evaluated. Attribute 2.3B to IFM/Inception42’s convention, not a new Google disclosure: Google calls 2.3B effective. Exact per-token participation and modality coverage remain unspecified. No count is computed by copying totals, subtracting embeddings or adding encoders. AA/fairseq2 leads contain material architecture contradictions.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only Transformer with 35 layers, per-layer embeddings, four local-attention layers per global layer and 20 layers sharing earlier K/V cache. Separate vision Transformer and audio encoder; no routed MoE experts.

context_window.note: Exact max_position_embeddings=131072; the card reports 128K tokens.

modalities.note: Add explicitly documented video input, processed as sampled image frames. Native image and audio encoders are present; output is text.

reasoning.note: Configurable thinking is explicitly documented for the instruction-tuned family including E2B.

tool_call.note: The card reports native function calling. This is a developer-reported capability; no local inference test is claimed.

description.value: Instruction-tuned dense Gemma 4 model with per-layer embeddings, text, image, audio and video inputs, text output, configurable thinking and function calling.
description.note: Replaces efficiency/deployment marketing with verified structure and capabilities.

patch.notes: Approximately 5.1043B complete usable-model parameters, including PLE, audio, vision and projectors; stored checkpoint values total about 5.1232B because unused shared-layer tensors remain. Active 2.3B applies IFM/Inception42’s E2B comparison convention to IT through Google’s documented shared base/IT architecture; the comparison omits the IT suffix. Google calls 2.3B effective. Exact per-token and modality coverage are unspecified. Tied embeddings count once; separate MTP assistant excluded. Video uses image frames. April 2, 2026 is retained from contemporaneous release evidence; the current family chronology says March 31.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retained the verified 5.1043B complete usable-model total. Nominal 2.3B active is inferred for IT from IFM/Inception42’s E2B comparison convention and Google’s explicit base relationship with identical configurations; the Jais table itself omits IT. Google’s effective-size terminology remains distinct. All unrelated assessments and earlier corrections are preserved.
